title: Small ramification and the base cases for Serre modularity, Part II: low-degree Hodge obstructions
summary: A higher-cohomology continuation of the everywhere-good-reduction obstruction. Starting from existing discriminant, Fontaine–Laffaille and comparison theories, it plans Fontaine’s higher-weight torsion ramification estimate and the global 7-adic cyclotomic filtration. These yield off-diagonal Hodge vanishing through total degree three for proper smooth rational schemes with unramified Witt-ring scheme models at every prime, and the resulting K3 bad-reduction obstruction.
readme: The normative reader document is research/blueprint/readmes/SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCasesPartII.md. All statements use HT(χ)=+1, geometric Frobenius for cohomological purity and v₀(p)=1. This extension adds the 1993 higher-weight argument beyond R25.1–R25.3; finite-flat group schemes, period rings, comparison functors, general purity, K3 definitions and Enriques covers keep their existing owners. Author-scan pagination is distinguished from the proceedings pagination. Every layer is a target-level plan, with explicit supplier contracts and no implementation claim.

stages.title: Unramified local models and cohomology
stages.description: Define the existential proper smooth scheme models over W(F̄_p), with generic-fibre isomorphism, for every p. From them obtain the unramified-away-from-seven, crystalline-at-seven dual cohomology representation, the exact Hodge–Tate sign dictionary and smooth proper purity. Models over ramified extensions or algebraic spaces alone do not satisfy this input.

stages.title: Higher-weight torsion crystalline ramification
stages.description: For unramified K=W(k)[1/p], perfect k, 0<r<p−1 and a killed-p Fontaine–Laffaille module of weights [0,r], construct the filtered valuation truncations and their solution functor. Prove unique polynomial solution lifting, comparison with the imported torsion crystalline representation, the field-detection criterion and the approximate-embedding bound. Deduce the strict normalized different inequality v₀(𝔇)<1+r/(p−1), and export it for killed-p crystalline subquotients. Import the FL objects and generic ramification criterion. The positive range excludes p=2.

stages.title: The global crystalline filtration at seven
stages.description: Define the finite global crystalline category of all 7-power exponents and the descending character filtration. Prove trivial-endpoint extension rigidity, the four simple objects F_7(i), the ordered mod-seven extension splitting except possibly quotient 1/sub χ³, the no-trivial-quotient decomposition and the exhaustive finite filtration. Pass through stable lattices and compact inverse limits to the rational filtration of any globally unramified-outside-seven representation crystalline at seven of weights [0,3]. Import certified discriminant bounds from the base roadmap.

stages.title: Low-degree cohomology and Hodge vanishing
stages.description: For proper smooth X/Q with all the Witt scheme models, combine the global filtration and proper smooth purity to prove H^1_et=H^3_et=0 and H^2_et≅Q_7(−1)^b. Via Hodge–Tate comparison prove H^j(X,Ω_X^i)=0 for i≠j and i+j≤3. Include the global Z-model and independent Z_p-model specializations, without converses or a degree-four assertion.

stages.title: K3 obstruction and boundary examples
stages.description: Use the shared projective geometric K3 predicate and coherent base change to prove h^{2,0}=1, hence the existence of a bad prime over W(F̄_p). Projective Z_p-scheme models supplied by the Enriques consumer meet the hypothesis. Check projective spaces and diagonal Hodge classes, and the strict total-degree restriction. Proper/projective comparison for a more general intrinsic K3 input belongs to the K3 owner; canonical covers and twisting belong to the Enriques owner.
